identity.name: Node systemd Service + Cron Reload Persistence (T1543.002 / T1053.003)
identity.summary: After node compromise an operator builds a self-reloading foothold: a systemd unit (Restart=always, /tmp ExecStart), daemon-reload + enable --now, plus a */10 root cron watchdog that re-enables the unit if removed. Cortex fires the unit-write, daemon-reload-then-enable, and cron-watchdog BIOCs into one persistence incident — a focused systemd variant distinct from TTP-2026-0034.
identity.description: systemd service persistence (T1543.002) is the most durable foothold on a modern Linux node: unlike a one-off cron entry, a service unit survives reboots, restarts on failure, and — when paired with a cron-driven watchdog (T1053.003) — re-installs itself after eviction, defeating a single cleanup. This card gives the CDR plane a focused, systemd-centric detection variant of persistence (deliberately narrower and deeper than TTP-2026-0034 / SIM-EDR-003, which sprays five different mechanisms): it concentrates on the operationally-important systemd + cron-reload watchdog combination that node-resident cryptojacking and access-broker tooling actually use. The chain: (1) write a `.service` unit into /etc/systemd/system with `Restart=always` and an `ExecStart` pointing at a hidden /tmp binary; (2) run `systemctl daemon-reload` immediately followed by `systemctl enable --now` on the new unit — the daemon-reload-then-enable sequence that is the highest-signal systemd-persistence behaviour; (3) install a root crontab `*/10` job that re-writes and re-enables the unit if it disappears (the self-healing watchdog). SAFE-MODE: the ExecStart and crontab reference an inert `/tmp/.cortexsim_node_beacon` marker (no payload runs), and cleanup disables+removes the unit, strips the crontab line, and reloads the daemon. The detection model maps each behaviour to a dedicated Cortex BIOC: a systemd-unit-file-write BIOC, a `daemon-reload`→`enable` process-sequence BIOC (the differentiator vs a benign unit edit), and a cron-watchdog BIOC keyed on the systemctl-in-crontab pattern. Validation XQL confirms each in xdr_data, IOC signatures pin the unit name and beacon path, and a correlation rule fuses the unit write, the enable sequence, and the cron watchdog from one node into a single persistence incident.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service

execution.framework_reference_id: T1543.002 — systemd unit write + daemon-reload/enable + cron-reload watchdog (SAFE-MODE inert beacon)

prerequisites.description: Cortex Cloud runtime defender or Cortex XDR Linux agent installed and reporting on the node.
prerequisites.check_command: systemctl is-active cortex-agent || ps aux | grep -i defender

prerequisites.description: Root on the node (systemd unit install + daemon-reload require it). Lab only.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE node persistence — ExecStart/crontab reference an inert marker, no payload runs.
# step-1: write a systemd service unit with Restart=always + /tmp ExecStart (T1543.002)
cat > /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-node.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=cortexsim node beacon (SAFE-MODE)
[Service]
ExecStart=/tmp/.cortexsim_node_beacon
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
# step-2: daemon-reload THEN enable --now (the high-signal systemd-persistence sequence)
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now cortexsim-node.service 2>/dev/null || true
# step-3: cron watchdog that re-installs+re-enables the unit if removed (T1053.003)
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '*/10 * * * * systemctl is-enabled cortexsim-node.service || systemctl enable --now cortexsim-node.service') | crontab -

expected_artifacts.description: systemd unit file written into /etc/systemd/system with Restart=always and a /tmp ExecStart.
systemctl daemon-reload immediately followed by systemctl enable on the new unit.
Root crontab entry that re-enables the unit (self-healing watchdog).

cleanup.code:
systemctl disable --now cortexsim-node.service 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-node.service
systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null || true
crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v cortexsim-node.service | crontab - 2>/dev/null || true
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-006 cleanup complete — unit disabled+removed, cron watchdog stripped, daemon reloaded'

iocs.context: systemd service unit installed for node persistence with Restart=always and a /tmp ExecStart.
Hidden /tmp ExecStart target referenced by the persistence unit and the cron watchdog.

biocs.name: CDR-006 Systemd Unit Written With Restart Always And Tmp ExecStart
biocs.description: A .service unit is written into a systemd unit directory with an ExecStart in /tmp or /dev/shm — the systemd-persistence file-write fingerprint (T1543.002). Narrower and deeper than the EDR-003 generic systemd BIOC.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_path contains ".service"
| filter action_file_path contains_any ("/etc/systemd/system", "/usr/lib/systemd/system", "/run/systemd/system", "/.config/systemd")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, container_id, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path

biocs.name: CDR-006 Systemd Daemon-Reload Then Enable New Unit Sequence
biocs.description: systemctl daemon-reload immediately followed by systemctl enable/start of a freshly-written unit — the high-signal systemd-persistence process sequence that distinguishes malicious unit install from a benign package edit (T1543.002).
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "systemctl"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("daemon-reload", "enable", "--now", "start")
| comp count() as systemctl_calls, values(action_process_image_command_line) as cmds by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter systemctl_calls >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, systemctl_calls, cmds

biocs.name: CDR-006 Cron Watchdog Re-Enabling Systemd Unit
biocs.description: A crontab entry that invokes systemctl to re-enable a service unit — the self-healing cron watchdog that re-installs systemd persistence after eviction (T1053.003).
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and actor_process_image_name = "crontab" and action_process_image_command_line contains "systemctl") or (event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path contains_any ("/var/spool/cron", "/etc/cron"))
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("systemctl", "enable", "is-enabled", ".service") or action_file_path contains "cron"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line, action_file_path

xql_queries.name: CDR-006 Validate Systemd Persistence Unit Write
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path contains ".service"
| filter action_file_path contains_any ("/etc/systemd/system", "/usr/lib/systemd/system", "/run/systemd/system")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, container_id, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path

xql_queries.name: CDR-006 Validate daemon-reload Then enable Sequence
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "systemctl" and action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("daemon-reload", "enable", "--now")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: CDR-006 Validate Cron Watchdog Re-Enabling Unit
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "crontab" and action_process_image_command_line contains "systemctl"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: CDR-006 Hunt Restart-Always Units With Untrusted ExecStart Across Nodes
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path contains "/etc/systemd/system" and action_file_path contains ".service"
| comp count() as unit_writes, count_distinct(agent_hostname) as nodes by actor_process_image_name, action_file_path
| sort desc unit_writes
| fields actor_process_image_name, action_file_path, unit_writes, nodes

correlation_rules.name: Persistence — Node systemd Unit + Self-Healing Cron Watchdog (Same Node)
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(CDR-006 Systemd Unit Written With Restart Always And Tmp ExecStart) AND (BIOC(CDR-006 Systemd Daemon-Reload Then Enable New Unit Sequence) OR BIOC(CDR-006 Cron Watchdog Re-Enabling Systemd Unit)) — fuses the unit write, the enable sequence, and the cron watchdog from one node into a single persistence incident.

use_cases.name: Persistence Mechanism Detection — Node systemd + Cron Watchdog
use_cases.description: Detect and evict a self-healing node persistence foothold (systemd service unit + cron-reload watchdog) — a focused systemd-centric variant distinct from the broad multi-mechanism EDR card.

test_cases.objective: The unit write, the daemon-reload/enable sequence, and the cron watchdog each fire their Cortex BIOC.
preconditions: Cortex Cloud runtime defender or Cortex XDR Linux agent >= 8.4.0 reporting on the node.
BIOCs from this card imported and enabled.
steps: Run SIM-CDR-006 steps 1-3 on the node.
Observe the per-stage BIOC alerts in the Cortex console.
success_criteria: BIOC `CDR-006 Systemd Unit Written With Restart Always And Tmp ExecStart` fires on the unit write.
BIOC `CDR-006 Systemd Daemon-Reload Then Enable New Unit Sequence` fires within 60s.
All three XQL validation queries return >= 1 row.

test_cases.objective: The persistence behaviours stitch into one incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-CDR-0006` groups the behaviours on one node into a single persistence incident.
The XSOAR eviction playbook is offered, including stripping the cron watchdog.

preventive_controls: Restrict systemd unit directories to root and audit unit-file writes with auditd/fapolicyd.
Disallow crontab on application/runtime nodes and alert on systemctl invoked from cron.
Enforce a runtime binary allowlist so a /tmp ExecStart target can never execute.
detection_engineering: Alert on .service writes into systemd unit dirs with Restart=always and an ExecStart outside trusted paths.
Alert on the daemon-reload→enable process sequence for a freshly-written unit (the malicious-install fingerprint).
Alert on crontab entries that invoke systemctl enable/is-enabled (the self-healing watchdog), and correlate all three into one incident.
